Hi Taylor / Sofia,

Thanks again for the call today — really useful to understand Acme's latency targets and the mix of workloads. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Low-latency chat frontend: target p95 <= 300ms for short responses (~64 tokens) for 200 concurrent users during peak window.
- Bulk embedding/reranker pipelines: nightly batch of ~3M texts, and live reranks at ~20 req/s.
- High-throughput inference for long-context summarization jobs (avg 1,024 tokens output) scheduled as background jobs.
- Authentication: customer-managed SSO + KMS for keys (Private/Dedicated mode).
- Routing: we should be able to route customer-facing traffic to dedicated pool and fallback to hosted variants if capacity constrained.

Integration/architecture items to cover (what we propose to scope for the tech deep-dive):
- SDK setup & auth: API keys, OAuth for service-to-service, and KMS integration for secrets.
- Routing and fallback policies: model pinning, regional failover, cost-tier routing.
- Structured output & tool calling: support for function-calling + deterministic JSON schemas for the chat UI.
- Embeddings & rerankers: recommendation for separate GPU pool vs shared worker nodes and batching strategies.
- Autoscaling, throughput sizing & queues: baseline nodes, max burst capacity, request queue sizing and concurrency limits per GPU.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (fill the highlighted sheets with your 95/99 p50/p95 targets, typical request size, and batch jobs). I also dropped a one-page scope doc (acme-integration-scope.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
1) You fill the sizing template and add any missing workload numbers (if you can share by EOD Tuesday, we’ll pre-populate recommendations).
2) Book a 60m technical deep-dive (link below) — we’ll bring Aditya (runtime) and Dev (infra).
3) We’ll return a recommended Dedicated capacity configuration (node types, baseline vs autoscale policy, concurrency settings, queue depth) and a draft mutual action plan within 3 business days of the deep-dive.

Looping in a couple of quick engineering notes from the runtime side — copying the external thread so Acme has visibility. High-level recommendations based on the numbers Marissa captured + Taylor’s follow-ups: 

Autoscaling / baseline sizing:
- Baseline: 2 dedicated nodes (NVIDIA A10 / equivalent) to handle steady traffic + reliability. This gives headroom for background jobs and small bursts.
- Autoscale up to 8 nodes for peak concurrency/burst (policy: scale by average CPU/GPU utilization and incoming request queue length with a 30s evaluation window).
- Burst capacity: allow an extra 2 nodes as pre-warmed for short spikes (fast boot images).

Concurrency & per-GPU limits:
- Concurrency per GPU: for chat-like short responses we recommend 12–16 concurrent sessions per GPU for p95 <= 300ms (depends on model and quantization).
- For long-context summarization (1k tokens out): schedule on dedicated longer-job workers with lower concurrency (2–4 per GPU) to avoid blocking short requests.

Queues / throttling:
- Request queue depth: 200–500 slots for user-facing requests; implement priority queues so interactive traffic is served before batch embeddings.
- Backpressure: circuit-breaker to reject requests with 429 when queue depth > 400 or when model latency exceeds 800ms.

Batching & embeddings:
- Run nightly embedding jobs on separate node pool (same instance class but isolated) with high batch sizes (up to 2048) to maximize throughput.
- Live rerankers at ~20 req/s can run on the interactive pool with batching window ~50–100ms to keep latency within p95 targets.

Other integration notes:
- Auth: support for customer-managed KMS + service accounts. We recommend short-lived tokens for runtime calls and a refresh flow for long-running jobs.
- Routing/fallback: model pinning to dedicated pool; fallback path to hosted models (lower-cost) only when nodes unavailable — we can add circuit-breaker policies and a traffic shadowing step during rollouts.
- Tool-calling / structured output: runtime supports function-calling with strict JSON schema enforcement; recommend schema validation at the client before sending to avoid expensive re-runs.

Open items for deep-dive:
- Confirm exact model family (LLM size & quantization) — this materially changes per-GPU throughput.
- Finalize percentage of traffic that can tolerate fallback to hosted (for cost vs reliability tradeoffs).
- Agree on RPO/RTO for batch embedding jobs (how tolerant you are to retries/slower completion).

Happy to go deeper on any bullet in the tech call. I’ll draft a recommended node/policy config once we have the filled sizing sheet and selected model.

- Aditya
